_comment: WHAT THIS MEASURES, and what it cannot.
The page served here carries the SEEDED PLACEHOLDER GLB — about 10 KB. A real
garment is 8-40 MB. So this run says nothing whatsoever about how heavy a
production page is, and a green badge must never be read that way. The budget
that applies to real models is enforced where they actually pass through:
SIZE_WARNING_BYTES in the shrink report the owner reads, and GLB_HARD_MAX_BYTES
in the CMS upload guard.
What this job DOES protect is the application shell — scripts, CSS, fonts —
which is byte-for-byte the same in production as it is here. So the budgets
below are scoped to exactly that, and `total-byte-weight` was removed: it
conflated the shell with the model and made a 2.1 MB ceiling look like a
statement about the live page.
The category scores stay `warn`. They swung 0.64 / 0.88 / 0.87 across three
local runs of the identical build on 2026-08-01 — 24 points of noise — so
gating on them would block releases at random. The byte budgets are
deterministic and are therefore the parts that fail the build.
MEASURED 2026-08-03 on the committed build, transfer sizes, identical across
all three runs:
stylesheet     20,583 B   budget    30,000  (+46%)
The headroom is deliberately small. A first draft of these used 400 KB and
120 KB — 3.5x and 6x the real figures — which would have passed through any
regression short of a catastrophe and told nobody anything. CSS gets the
loosest ratio because a genuine design change moves it most.
CHANGED 2026-09-24 BY THE OWNER'S DECISION: the website's menu bar on the viewer. Stylesheet transfer measured 29,664 -> 34,539 B (lhci, three identical runs); budget 30,000 -> 34,875.
